newsitem.title: MEXICO: Spanish PM offers Mexico help to fight terrorism.
newsitem.headline: Spanish PM offers Mexico help to fight terrorism.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar pledged on Friday to help Mexico fight "terrorism" after recent attacks by a new rebel group.
"If Mexico needs whatever help from Spain, it will have it," Aznar told reporters during a three-day visit to Mexico, the second leg of a Latin American tour by the Spanish leader.
"Terrorism is one of the main threats to our societies ... and between friendly nations there should be no doubt in helping to fight it," Aznar added.

Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo has labeled as "terrorists" the Popular Revolutionary Army, a new guerrilla group that appeared two months ago calling for the overthrow of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party.

Terrorism was on the agenda during talks between Zedillo and Aznar on Thursday, the Spanish leader said. Spain has in the past asked Mexico to extradite former members of the Basque separatist group ETA who have sought refuge here.

Aznar, whose conservative government has been in power since May, said the extradition request was not raised again during his meetings with Zedillo but he said both sides discussed recent changes to a bilateral extradition treaty that were "aimed in that direction."

He also said Spain would vigorously promote Mexico's wish for a free-trade agreement with the European Union, a request blocked by several European countries that say Mexican imports to Europe might cost jobs.
